svg.title: UKF vs Particle Filter
svg.desc: UKF collapses the posterior into one Gaussian; the particle filter keeps its shape with weighted samples, at the price of particle count and the curse of dimensionality.
svg.text: UKF vs particle filter — one Gaussian vs the shape of a sample
2m+1 deterministic points vs N random weighted samples
Linear in dimension m — very cheap
Hundreds to tens of thousands of random samples
Converges to the true posterior as N grows
Puts the mass midway between the two modes
Even the valley between modes survives
Points grow in proportion to the dimension
The cost stays manageable even in high dimensions
The particles needed explode with dimension
In high dimensions particles cannot cover the posterior
UKF collapses the posterior into one Gaussian; the particle filter keeps its shape.
Expressiveness costs particles and scales with dimension — PF for low-dimensional multimodality, UKF for high-dimensional mild nonlinearity.
Propose from the state equation and
